data: Longest-serving engine in spaceflight — the first hydrogen upper stage
Engine registry (PRD-032). Public-source nominal specs; NASA imagery.
Hydrogen upper stage, six decades and counting

The RL10 introduced the expander cycle to spaceflight: propellant flows through the nozzle and chamber walls, picks up heat, and drives the turbopump before it ever reaches the combustion chamber — no separate gas generator required. First flown in November 1963 on the Centaur upper stage, the RL10 family has since powered upper stages for Atlas, Delta, and Vulcan missions. Its longevity is the record; no other rocket engine family has remained in continuous production and flight for as long, evolving through block upgrades while the core thermodynamic concept stays intact.
